findings.issue: Card assembly is duplicated between the home load and cardsFor (app/src/lib/server/api.ts:80-100), so behaviour changes to cards (sprite source, name resolution, new badge) must land in two places.
findings.suggestion: Have the home load build cards through a shared helper (e.g. extend cardsFor or extract a makeCard), keeping one definition of what a card is.

findings.issue: typeLabels is constructed inline even though getTypeLabels() in api.ts does exactly this.
findings.suggestion: Import getTypeLabels() and delete the local Map construction.

findings.issue: The 'Hidden ability' presentation is specific to the abilities page but lives in the generic CardList via Card.hidden, coupling the shared component to one route and hindering removal.
findings.suggestion: Accept an optional snippet/slot for per-list extras, or pass the hidden flag as a label computed by the caller so CardList stays generic.

findings.issue: Cache TTL and eviction policy are constants inside api.ts; fine today, but any multi-policy caching change means editing the fetch internals.
findings.suggestion: Consider a small configurable cache wrapper so TTL/eviction can change without touching fetchApi's body.

findings.issue: The Move interface overlaps with the one in app/src/routes/moves/[name]/+page.server.ts:8-19; shared fields (type, power, accuracy, pp) are declared twice.
findings.suggestion: Per-route interface declarations are defensible, but the common API shapes could live in #lib/server/api.ts next to the other resource interfaces.

findings.issue: Row keys include the loop index ('${row.name}-${row.level}-${i}'), weakening keyed reconciliation if rows are ever reordered.
findings.suggestion: Key on a stable composite (name+method+level) without the index, or ensure uniqueness upstream.

summary: A clean, fully current SvelteKit 3 codebase with excellent server/client separation, centralized 404/formatting/caching logic, and components that stretch to the app's real variation. The main editability cost is duplicated card assembly (home load vs cardsFor) and one ability-specific concern threaded through the shared Card type and CardList. Most changes land in one obvious place; removing a feature requires a small, findable scatter of edits.
